title: Be Committed to Family Worship
author: Justin Myko Agpangan
summary: Justin Myko Agpangan argues that Christian husbands and fathers should lead regular family worship as a central part of their spiritual leadership in the home. He starts from Paul's qualifications for elders in 1 Timothy 3, reasoning that the household-management and faithfulness standards set for elders apply in principle to every Christian man, since the family functions like a little church. From there he describes men as prophets to their wives and children, not in a predictive sense, but as those responsible for teaching, applying and modelling Scripture at home. The second half is practical. Agpangan insists family worship is less about difficulty than commitment and consistency: begin with a short book such as Colossians, read a chapter or paragraph, explain and apply it, invite wives and children to share what struck them, and close in prayer. He describes his own practice of at least fifteen minutes nightly with his wife, warns against treating family worship as a leftover while also cautioning against neglecting other responsibilities, and concludes that family worship shows that God rules the home through His Word.
points: Agpangan grounds household spiritual leadership in 1 Timothy 3, arguing elder qualifications about managing the home apply to all Christian husbands and fathers.
He frames husbands as prophets in the sense of speaking and applying the Bible to their families while living out what they teach.
Family worship requires commitment and consistency more than expertise, and he urges men to equip themselves through study and good books rather than lead passively.
His method: choose a short biblical book, read a chapter or paragraph, explain and apply it, ask family members what struck them, and end in prayer.
Timing and length can flex with family circumstances (mealtimes, mornings or nights), but it should be a priority rather than a leftover.
quotes: These qualifications touch the attitudes and the behaviors of aspiring men with how they live out their faith at home. Elders are not just the only one exemplifying these qualifications. These should also be true to all genuine followers of Jesus Christ.

In light of that, one of the best ways to reflect Jesus to our wives and children (for others and prayerfully for me in the future, Lord willing) is through family worship, setting an example through our words and also in our actions. We should be committed to this means of grace at home.
We don't just impart information. We also teach how to apply the Bible in the lives of our wives and children (for others who have children). We are not just merely vessels of information.
This is actually not that hard to do. This requires more commitment and consistency from us. But we should not be afraid or be intimidated.

Me and my wife try to have our family worship every day at night at least fifteen minutes daily. There are days when we go up to forty five minutes especially in days when we have more time to free up for family worship. I don't mean to suggest that we should treat family worship like a leftover.

Then after that seek to explain and apply the passage. Ask your wife or your children the things that struck them from the passage. This could be done in an interactive way. And that's good because it's a way also to bond with each other.
And over time, God always uses His Word to transform us to be more like Jesus for His glory and the good of others, especially the good of our families. So let us be committed to family worship.
